=={{header|Ada}}==
;Program Text
* Ada syntax is descended from Pascal and delimits program blocks with English words.
* Ada is completely case-insensitive, so `if` and `IF` are the same reserved word and `x` and `X` are the same variable.
* Reserved words (e.g. `if`,`for`, `function`, `begin`) are written in all lowercase.
* Program blocks are expected to end with the same keyword or label (e.g. `if`...`end if;`)
* Identifiers (e.g. variables, types, functions, packages) use Capital_Snake_Case
* Use full English words rather than abbreviations (e.g. `Time_Of_Day` rather than `TOD`)
* Use custom types to encode information about variables rather than tagging conventions (e.g. `Paid : Amount` instead of `Paid_Amount : Integer`
* Avoid using the same identifier for different syntactic elements (e.g. don't have both a type and variable named `Day`)
* Ada supports function overloading, so multiple functions with the same name and different arguments are encouraged.

For example:
<syntaxhighlight lang="ada">
function Max (Left, Right : Integer) return Integer is
begin
   if Left < Right then
      return Right;
   else
      return Left;
   end if;
end Max;
</syntaxhighlight>

;File Names
Though not a language requirement, every package should have a spec file `.ads` and containing publicly visible declarations and a body file `.adb` containing matching definitions with file names matching the package name in lowercase.

In `my_package.ads`:
<syntaxhighlight lang="ada">
package My_Package is
...
end My_Package;
</syntaxhighlight>

In `my_package.adb`:
<syntaxhighlight lang="ada">
package body My_Package is
...
end My_Package;
</syntaxhighlight>
